title: Implement File Transfers and Feature Authorization
content:
This section reuses existing browser and API evidence from sections 5.7.2, 5.8.2, 5.10.2, and 5.10.3 to avoid repeating screenshots.
Objective Implement presigned upload/download, Favorites, Tags, Trash, and sharing with server-side checks.
Implementation steps Follow the steps in order. Read the action, its explanation, and the expected check before moving to the next step.
Step 1: In backend/src/index.mjs, build the S3 key from Cognito In backend/src/index.mjs, build the S3 key from Cognito sub and a server-generated ID; validate file type/size before returning a PUT URL. On completion, use HeadObject before writing metadata.
Step 2: For download, sharing, favorites, and Trash, identify the For download, sharing, favorites, and Trash, identify the caller from claims and check permissions before issuing URLs or changing records. The frontend calls routes through src/services/documentService.js.
Step 3: Favorites are a user/document relation Favorites are a user/document relation; Trash is a soft delete using deletedAt, and restore removes that attribute. Hard delete must coordinate the S3 object, metadata, shares, and favorites.
Step 4: Share creation resolves email to Cognito sub Share creation resolves email to Cognito sub; only the owner can grant/revoke access. A Viewer can read/download an active shared file; an issued URL remains usable until it expires.
Step 5: After Lambda changes, build/deploy with SAM After Lambda changes, build/deploy with SAM. The frontend uses API URL and Cognito IDs from Outputs; it never accesses DynamoDB/S3 with browser credentials.
Example: create the key and upload URL The key is built from the user’s sub and a server-generated document ID; the browser does not choose the key:
const documentId = randomUUID(); const s3Key = `users/${caller.sub}/documents/${documentId}`; const uploadUrl = await getSignedUrl(s3, new PutObjectCommand({ Bucket: process.env.DOCUMENTS_BUCKET, Key: s3Key, ContentType: contentType, Metadata: { "document-id": documentId }, }), { expiresIn: 300 }); Verified behavior and evidence Presigned upload and download: The successful S3 upload, saved document metadata, and download flow are recorded in section 5.8.2. Resource authorization: Section 5.7.2 records the unauthenticated 401 and the signed-in second account receiving 404 for an owner’s unshared document. Sharing: The recipient’s Shared With Me view and download interaction are recorded in section 5.10.2. A direct recipient download is also recorded in section 5.8.2. Favorites, metadata, and Trash/restore: These results are recorded in sections 5.8.2 and 5.10.3. The local upload form rejected a file over its displayed 20 MB limit, and a separate authenticated request verified that the deployed POST /documents/upload-url rejects 20 MiB + 1 byte with HTTP 400 before issuing an S3 upload URL; see section 5.10.1.
Expected result Document features use backend data and permissions are enforced in Lambda.
Troubleshooting A Viewer must not edit, share onward, or delete another user’s document. Cross-service S3/DynamoDB operations are not automatically atomic; document recovery for partial failures.

Workshop: Building UniCloud DMS on AWS This workshop guides learners from the existing React/Vite frontend to an AWS-backed document-management application.
How to follow the workshop For a first-time setup, follow the sequence below. Sections 5.3–5.7 explain and verify each service; you do not need to create these resources one by one in the Console, because SAM provisions the resources described in section 5.1.3.
Complete 5.1 Prerequisites to install the tools and prepare an AWS account. Read 5.2 Backend Design to understand the data flow and model before deployment. Follow 5.1.3 AWS SAM Backend Deployment Runbook to create the backend and record its Outputs. Use sections 5.3–5.7 to compare Cognito, DynamoDB, S3, Lambda, and API Gateway with the deployed stack. Follow 5.8 Frontend Integration and 5.9 AWS Amplify Hosting, then run the checks in section 5.10. Follow 5.12 Cleanup only after saving evidence and when the application is no longer needed. The screenshots in section 5 record a previous completed deployment. The project’s AWS resources were deleted on November 19, 2026. Learners must deploy a new stack in their own account/Region and must not reuse IDs or URLs shown in screenshots.
Completed and verified Created the Cognito User Pool and public web app client; signed up and signed in with real Cognito accounts. Deployed the HTTP API, Lambda functions, private S3 bucket, and three DynamoDB tables. The tables and their access indexes are recorded in sections 5.4.1 and 5.4.2. Verified authenticated document-list requests (200), an unauthenticated request (401), and a logged-in second user requesting an unshared document (404). Verified upload, metadata persistence, download, Favorites, Trash/restore, sharing, recipient visibility/download, category filtering, tag search, and Vietnamese/English interface selection. Evidence is distributed across sections 5.7.2, 5.8.2, and 5.10. Configured the S3 bucket as private with default SSE-S3 encryption and added browser CORS rules for local and Amplify origins. Current operational notes The local upload form and deployed upload API both rejected a file over the 20 MiB limit; section 5.10.1 includes the API response for a 20 MiB + 1 byte request (400). The IAM screenshots confirm that the Lambda role had AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole and DmsDocumentRuntimeAccess attached. The runtime policy source scopes permissions to project resources, and protected document operations were exercised. The deployed architecture diagram and data-model design are included. Billing was captured on November 18, 2026; the November bill was still pending at that time and was not a final invoice. AWS project resources were cleaned up on November 19, 2026. The screenshots in sections 5.12.1 and 5.12.2 show the actual cleanup steps and resulting console states, while also serving as a step-by-step guide.
